title: 60-Second Alliance Reset
concept: A one-minute reset for when winning has replaced connecting. It’s designed to stop the damage fast; then you book proper time to work it out. We’d save it for the bad moments, not every disagreement.
whenToUse: When you’re still in the room together, it has turned into a fight to win, and you’re both willing to stop for one minute before anyone needs a longer pause.
steps: Stop — let go of winning or solving it for now.
Say it — “I want to connect, not fight.”
Touch (only if welcome) — keep it brief and leave it at that.
Breathe — take three slow breaths together.
Return — pick an exact time to keep talking.

phrases.text: I want to connect, not fight.
I’m stopping so we don’t do damage.

working: They’re mid-row over the holiday budget. A: “I’m stopping. I want to connect, not fight.” A puts a hand on B’s shoulder, if it’s welcome, and they both take three breaths. A asks, “Can we talk at 8pm?” and B agrees. The budget waits till 8.
notWorking: B uses the reset to shut the conversation down for good: “60-second reset — I’m done,” with no time to come back. That’s just walking away with extra steps.
activity: Practise the five steps on a fake topic (“dishes”) three times while you’re both calm. Agree on the phrase you’ll actually use.
